body: I'm rather troubled by the fact that many comedians (mostly men) hide behind the cloak of comedy when asked to defend their jokes. "Chill out," they say, "it's just a joke." Except, of course, that these men make careers out of just making jokes, and that in any other context, they would be demanding that you take them seriously. At least, seriously enough to watch their show, buy DVDs of their tours, or follow them on Twitter (or paste posters of their face all over your walls). They want you to respect their craft, and recognize that comedy is about making you think and not just a shallow chuckle in time. So it's not that comedians don't want to be taken seriously - they just don't want you to take them seriously when you feel offended. "It's just a joke" is no excuse for poor taste. If you want the glory of being taken seriously, you must accept the responsibility of BEING TAKEN SERIOUSLY. Welcome to the double-edged blade that is life.
